# About Nina

I graduated from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) with a B.S. in Human Biology and Society in March 2025 with Cum Laude Honors. At UCLA, I was involved in Nueroscience research, worked as an EMT in private transport, and mentor for younger students in the HBS major. Here, I became very interested into social determinants of health and understanding why certain individuals got care over others as I watched these disparities play out in real life as an EMT. 

I am currently a Columbia Mailman School of Public Health Candidate in Epidemiology with a certificate in Applied Data Science and Biostatistics. Here at Mailman, I work as a Research Assistant to improve cervical cancer screening. I am also Vice President of the Mailman Journalism Club where I run the podcast "Kind of a Big Health Deal" to bring conversations of health outside academia by interviewing a variety of Public Health Leaders and highlight community intiatives. I volunteer in the community with Coach Dave, remotely as a Helpline Volunteer with AZLA, and previously with Read Ahead.

After Mailman, I hoping to attend Medical School in hopes of treating individuals and advocating for the communities they came from. I think having a background in Public Health will make me a better future physician.
